key_insight: Water transport in anion exchange membranes is bidirectionally coupled to swelling and mechanics, so hydration-dependent deformation changes the predicted diffusion response.
engineering_relevance: Accurate CO2-separation membrane design needs models that capture both concentration-dependent transport and mechanical feedback under nonuniform hydration.
method: Transient finite element model for water transport + deformation in Fumasep FAA-3-50 AEM
Includes concentration-dependent diffusivity, hygroscopic swelling, and nonlinear viscoelastic response
Compares uncoupled, one-way coupled, and fully coupled formulations
evidence_signal: The fully coupled model was validated against steady-state water-transport measurements across water-activity gradients and matched the observed hydration dependence best at intermediate hydration.
watch_item: The model is still primarily diffusion-driven, so mechanical coupling may be less critical in regimes where hydration gradients and deformation are weak.
paper_title: Modeling Transport and Mechanics in Anion Exchange Membranes to Optimize Continuous CO2 Separations
